audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph genealogy from Adam through Edom, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for primeval genealogy, nations, Ishmael and Keturah lines, Esau/Seir, Edomite kings and chiefs, gender visibility, ethnic reception, and anti-Amalek misuse.

verses.restored: Adam, Seth, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim/Dodanim.
Sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
Sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. Sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be mighty upon earth.
Mizraim fathered Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
Pathrusim, Casluhim—from whom Philistines came—and Caphtorim.
Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn and Heth,
also Jebusite, Amorite, Girgashite,
Hivite, Arkite, Sinite,
Arvadite, Zemarite, and Hamathite.
Sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech/Mash.
Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
To Eber two sons were born: name of one was Peleg, because in his days earth was divided; name of his brother was Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Ebal/Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.
Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah,
Eber, Peleg, Reu,
Serug, Nahor, Terah,
Abram, that is, Abraham.
Sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
These are their generations: firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad/Hadar, Tema,
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were sons of Ishmael.
Sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine/wife: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
Sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were descendants of Keturah.
Abraham fathered Isaac. Sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
Sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jaalam, and Korah.
Sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi/Zepho, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
Sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
Sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
Sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; Timna was Lotan's sister.
Sons of Shobal: Alian/Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi/Shepho, and Onam. Sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
Son of Anah: Dishon. Sons of Dishon: Hamran/Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
Sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These are kings who reigned in land of Edom before a king reigned over children of Israel: Bela son of Beor; name of his city was Dinhabah.
Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.
Jobab died, and Husham from land of Temanites reigned in his place.
Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who struck Midian in field of Moab, reigned in his place; name of his city was Avith.
Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.
Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehoboth by river reigned in his place.
Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.
Baal-hanan died, and Hadad/Hadar reigned in his place; name of his city was Pai/Pau, and name of his wife was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.
Hadad died. Chiefs of Edom were: chief Timna, chief Aliah/Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel and chief Iram. These were chiefs of Edom.

translation_notes: Genealogies are selective social memory, not complete biological records and not rankings of human worth.
Names later associated with nations must not be racialized or used to assign inherited guilt to modern peoples.
Ishmael, Keturah, Esau, Seir, and Edom are preserved within the family archive rather than erased from it.
Edomite kings are explicitly remembered before Israel had a king; Israel is not presented as the only people with history or political organization.
Timna, Mehetabel, Matred, Me-zahab, Keturah, and other named women show that women are present even when patrilineal form often obscures them.
Amalek in verse 36 is an ancestral name within an ancient genealogy and may never be mapped onto any living population.
Textual variants in names—including Rodanim/Dodanim and several Edomite names—require later Hebrew, Greek, and parallel-text audit.
safety_note: Do not use this genealogy to construct racial hierarchies, blood purity, nationalism, antisemitism, anti-Arab hatred, anti-Edomite typologies, or modern Amalek targeting. Every named lineage represents human communities whose descendants cannot inherit ancient blame.
